answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by weighting influence through interaction-graph diversity rather than headcount. Standing grows only from exchanges with many unrelated peers, so a cluster of fakes that mostly talk to each other forms a dense dune of self-referential links and earns little weight. When one member misbehaves, a ripple penalty spreads along its trust edges, discounting its whole clique, and every exchange is sealed with a rotating cipher key tied to long-term identity, so a puppet master cannot rebrand the clique under fresh names without rebuilding years of diverse ties.
